title: Ebla destroyed and its archive buried
description: The palace of Ebla burns, baking and preserving thousands of clay tablets that record the trade and diplomacy of one of the earliest Syrian kingdoms.

title: Hammurabi destroys Mari
description: The king of Babylon sacks the city on the Euphrates, ending its kingdom and burying a palace archive of some 20,000 tablets.

title: Ugaritic alphabet
description: Scribes in the port of Ugarit write their language with thirty cuneiform signs, one of the earliest known alphabets.

title: Battle of Qarqar
description: A coalition led by the kings of Damascus and Hamath checks the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III on the Orontes.

title: Assyria takes Damascus
description: Tiglath-Pileser III captures Damascus, ends the Aramean kingdom and turns its land into Assyrian provinces.

title: Syria becomes a Roman province
description: Pompey deposes the last Seleucid king and makes Syria a Roman province, which it remains for seven centuries.

title: Aurelian takes Palmyra
description: The emperor Aurelian defeats Queen Zenobia and captures her desert city, ending the Palmyrene state that had ruled the Roman East.

title: Battle of the Yarmuk
place: Yarmuk River, near the Golan Heights
description: The army of the Rashidun Caliphate defeats the Byzantines, and Syria passes permanently from Roman to Muslim rule.

title: Damascus becomes the Umayyad capital
description: Muawiya I, governor of Syria, becomes caliph and rules the Islamic empire from Damascus, founding the Umayyad dynasty.

title: Umayyad Mosque completed
description: The great mosque built by Caliph al-Walid I on the site of the cathedral of Saint John is finished, one of the oldest and largest mosques in the world.

title: Abbasids take Damascus
description: Abbasid forces capture the Umayyad capital after their victory on the Zab, and the centre of the caliphate moves from Syria to Iraq.

title: Sayf al-Dawla takes Aleppo
description: The Hamdanid prince makes Aleppo the capital of an emirate in northern Syria, known for its wars with Byzantium and for its court poets.

title: Siege of Damascus
description: The army of the Second Crusade attacks Damascus and withdraws after four days, the failure that ends the crusade.

title: Death of Saladin
description: The sultan who united Egypt and Syria and retook Jerusalem dies in Damascus, and his lands are divided among his family.

title: Mongols take Aleppo
description: Hulagu's army storms Aleppo after a week's siege and kills much of its population, and Damascus surrenders soon after.

title: Krak des Chevaliers falls to Baibars
description: The Mamluk sultan takes the greatest of the Crusader castles from the Knights Hospitaller after a siege of about a month.

title: Timur sacks Aleppo and Damascus
description: Timur defeats the Mamluks, sacks both cities and carries the craftsmen of Damascus off to Samarkand.

title: Battle of Marj Dabiq
description: The Ottoman sultan Selim I defeats and kills the Mamluk sultan, and Syria comes under Ottoman rule for four hundred years.

title: Damascus massacre
description: Rioters destroy the Christian quarter of Damascus and kill thousands of its inhabitants, leading the Ottoman government to punish local officials and France to send troops to the region.

title: Capture of Damascus
description: Australian cavalry and the Arab army of Prince Faisal enter Damascus, ending Ottoman rule in Syria.

title: Battle of Maysalun
description: French troops defeat the army of the Arab Kingdom of Syria proclaimed in March, expel King Faisal and begin the French Mandate.

title: Great Syrian Revolt begins
polity: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon
description: A Druze uprising led by Sultan al-Atrash spreads across Syria and is put down by France over two years, including a bombardment of Damascus.

title: Last French troops leave
description: The evacuation of the last French soldiers completes Syria's independence, and the day becomes the national holiday.

title: United Arab Republic proclaimed
description: Presidents Shukri al-Quwatli and Gamal Abdel Nasser merge Syria and Egypt into one state, which lasts until a Syrian coup in 1961.

title: Ba'ath Party takes power
description: Officers of the Ba'ath Party seize power in a coup, beginning six decades of Ba'athist rule.

title: Hafez al-Assad takes power
description: The defence minister removes his rivals in the Ba'ath Party in a bloodless coup and goes on to rule Syria for thirty years.

title: Hama massacre
description: The army besieges and shells Hama to crush an uprising by the Muslim Brotherhood, killing many thousands of people.

title: Uprising begins
description: Protests against the government spread from Daraa after security forces fire on demonstrators, the start of the Syrian civil war.

title: Ghouta chemical attack
description: Rockets carrying the nerve agent sarin hit opposition-held suburbs of Damascus and kill hundreds of people, after which Syria agrees to give up its chemical weapons.

title: Russian intervention begins
description: Russian aircraft begin air strikes in support of the Syrian government, which shifts the course of the civil war.

title: Government retakes Aleppo
description: The last rebel fighters and civilians are evacuated from eastern Aleppo, ending four years of fighting for Syria's largest city.

title: Islamic State loses its last territory
description: The Syrian Democratic Forces, backed by a coalition led by the United States, capture the last village held by the Islamic State.
